purpose: Make JSON the native machine-readable rail for TOPA while allowing large evidence dumps to be read, searched, transformed, hashed and reproduced without requiring full in-memory loading when line-oriented formats are used.

large_dump_policy.reason: One logical record per line allows deterministic record-by-record iteration, filtering and search with bounded memory.
large_dump_policy.monolithic_json_boundary: A top-level .json array/object is a single JSON document and the standard-library implementation parses it as one document. TOPA must not pretend that this is streaming. Very large arrays should be converted or exported as JSONL/NDJSON before heavy analysis.

compression.gzip: transparent UTF-8 streaming via Python gzip
compression.bzip2: transparent UTF-8 streaming via Python bz2

operations.read: iter_records(path) yields logical records; JSONL/NDJSON is line streamed.
operations.write_jsonl: JsonlWriter writes one canonicalized record per line to plain/gzip/bzip2 rails.
operations.inspect: validates the rail, counts records/types, records malformed lines and emits raw plus semantic SHA-256 receipts.
operations.search: case-insensitive substring and optional regex search over the whole record or a dotted field; matching records may be streamed into another compressed JSONL/NDJSON rail.
operations.convert: converts between supported rails while explicitly recording whether the output path is streaming or requires a monolithic JSON array in memory.
operations.self_test: tests plain and compressed JSON/JSONL/NDJSON round-trip, search and conversion.

provenance_contract.raw_byte_hash: SHA-256 of stored file bytes, therefore compression-sensitive.
provenance_contract.semantic_record_stream_hash: SHA-256 over canonical sort-key JSON representations of logical records separated by newline; useful for checking logical equivalence across compression containers.
provenance_contract.malformed_line_policy: strict by default; --skip-bad must be explicit and malformed-line samples remain in the receipt.
provenance_contract.missing_data_rule: Malformed or missing records are never silently fabricated or imputed by the I/O layer.

rules: A raw model score must be preserved exactly as produced and remain addressable after every calibration or transformation.
A calibrated output must be written to a different field/artifact and must carry the calibrator identity, training split, parameter state and provenance.
An uncalibrated model score must not be relabeled as a physical probability.
Ranking/discrimination metrics such as AUC do not prove probability calibration.
If a calibration mapping materially collapses score diversity, TOPA must flag the collapse and must not replace the raw distribution with that mapping.
Distribution-collapse thresholds belong to the preregistered experiment that uses the scores; they are not invented after seeing the target association.
Nuclear/UAP labels are forbidden from calibration selection when the classifier is supposed to estimate artifact quality independently of the nuclear hypothesis.

epistemic_guards: JSON validity is not scientific validity.
A hash proves byte or logical identity under the declared canonicalization, not truth of the represented claim.
Search hits are retrieval results, not independent witnesses.
Compression does not change evidentiary authority.
A model-generated field is not promoted merely because it is machine-readable.
